config.title: Type polymorphic React component props

intro.title: Type polymorphic React component props
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a flexible React component that can render as different HTML elements, like a button, link, or heading, while keeping full TypeScript type safety. You'll learn how to use TypeScript generics to define polymorphic props, allowing a single component to adapt its structure and behavior. The core concept involves typing a component's `as` prop to accept an element type string and dynamically inferring its props. You'll work with React's `ElementType`, TypeScript generics, and JSX to create a reusable, type-safe component.
intro.usecase: Polymorphic props are essential when building design systems and component libraries that need to work across different HTML elements. For example, a Button component might need to render as a <button>, <a>, or <div> depending on whether it triggers an action, navigates, or acts as a visual element. This pattern appears in navigation menus where items can be links or buttons, in data tables with clickable cells, and in card components that might need to be clickable or static. Mastering polymorphic props allows you to create flexible, reusable components that maintain type safety while adapting to various UI contexts.

objectives: Implement a polymorphic React component with TypeScript generics
Configure type-safe props that accept multiple HTML element types
Apply conditional rendering based on the polymorphic element type
Initialize and manipulate component state within polymorphic components
Bind event handlers to polymorphic elements with proper type inference
Construct type-safe ref forwarding for polymorphic components
Integrate polymorphic components into existing React applications

steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.title: Add an 'as' prop to specify element type
steps.instruction: Add an 'as' prop to the Box component's props interface with a default value of 'div'. The prop should be typed as a string literal union of possible HTML element names.
steps.hint: Extend the BoxProps interface to include an optional 'as' property with a union type like 'div' | 'span' | 'section' and set a default value in the function parameters.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Box component will have an 'as' prop that allows specifying different HTML element types, with 'div' as the default.
successCriteria: BoxProps interface includes an optional 'as' prop typed as a string literal union, and the component function parameters provide a default value of 'div'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure the 'as' prop is optional with a default value and properly typed as a union of element names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'as' prop wasn't added correctly. Check that it's included in the interface with proper TypeScript typing and has a default value.

steps.title: Type the 'as' prop with ElementType
steps.instruction: In the BoxProps interface, add an 'as' property typed as React.ElementType with a type parameter that allows string HTML element names like 'div', 'span', etc.
steps.hint: Use React.ElementType<string> to type the 'as' prop, which will accept any valid HTML element tag name as a string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The BoxProps interface now includes an 'as' prop typed as React.ElementType<string>, enabling the component to accept different HTML element types.
successCriteria: BoxProps interface has an 'as' property with type React.ElementType<string>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added an 'as' prop, but check the type. It should be React.ElementType<string> to accept string HTML element names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The 'as' prop is missing or incorrectly typed. Add 'as: React.ElementType<string>' to the BoxProps interface.

steps.title: Create a polymorphic component type
steps.instruction: Define a generic type called PolymorphicComponentProps that accepts two type parameters: As (defaulting to 'div') and Props (defaulting to {}). This type should include the 'as' prop typed as As and the rest of the props as Props & React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<As>.
steps.hint: Use TypeScript generics with default values. The type should combine the 'as' prop with the component's other props.
steps.expectedOutcome: A generic type that can infer props based on the 'as' prop value.
successCriteria: PolymorphicComponentProps type is defined with two generic parameters and properly combines the 'as' prop with component props.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your type includes both generic parameters and properly combines the 'as' prop with React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef.
steps.feedbackWrong: The type definition needs work. Review how to create generic types with default values in TypeScript.

steps.title: Apply the polymorphic type to Box props
steps.instruction: Update the Box component's props interface to use the PolymorphicComponentProps type with proper generics, replacing the existing BoxProps interface.
steps.hint: Replace the BoxProps interface with a type that uses PolymorphicComponentProps, specifying the generic type parameters appropriately.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Box component will have props typed with the polymorphic type, enabling it to accept an 'as' prop and forward props to the rendered element.
successCriteria: Box component uses PolymorphicComponentProps type with proper generics in its props definition.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the PolymorphicComponentProps type with the correct generic parameters for the Box component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The Box component's props still need to be updated to use the polymorphic type. Review how to apply generic types to component props.

steps.title: Extract props for the rendered element
steps.instruction: Inside the Box component, use ComponentPropsWithoutRef to extract the props for the element type specified by the 'as' prop. Add this as a type parameter to your PolymorphicComponentProps type.
steps.hint: You'll need to pass the element type (from the 'as' prop) to ComponentPropsWithoutRef to get its props. This should be added as a type parameter in your polymorphic type definition.
steps.expectedOutcome: The polymorphic type now includes props extracted from the element type specified by 'as', making the component truly type-safe for different HTML elements.
successCriteria: PolymorphicComponentProps type includes props extracted using ComponentPropsWithoutRef with the element type parameter
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using ComponentPropsWithoutRef with the element type parameter from your polymorphic type. Check that you've added it correctly to your type definition.
steps.feedbackWrong: The polymorphic type should include props extracted using ComponentPropsWithoutRef. Try using React.ComponentPropsWithoutRef<C> where C is your element type parameter.

steps.title: Implement the component rendering logic

steps.hint: Destructure the 'as' prop with a default value, then return the element using that variable as the JSX tag name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Box component will now render the element type specified by the 'as' prop instead of always rendering a <div>.
successCriteria: The Box component destructures the 'as' prop with a default value and returns the element using that variable as the JSX tag.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: The rendering logic isn't quite correct. Remember to destructure the 'as' prop and use it as the element type in the return statement.

steps.title: Test type safety with invalid props
steps.instruction: In the App component, add a Box component with 'as' set to 'button' but pass an invalid prop like 'href' to verify TypeScript catches the error.
steps.hint: Add a Box component inside the App's div with as='button' and include a prop that doesn't belong to button elements, such as href.
steps.analogousExample:

<Box as="button" href="#">Invalid button</Box>
steps.expectedOutcome: TypeScript will show an error for the invalid prop, confirming the type safety of the polymorphic component.
successCriteria: A Box component with as='button' and an invalid prop like 'href' is added to the App component, triggering a TypeScript error.
